unmapped: arms are strategic agents with private values-per-click v_i <= v_max reported as bids; reward of arm i is v_i times a Bernoulli(mu_i) click
mechanism must be (dominant-strategy) truthful and normalized, with payments computable only from observed clicks
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic \problem, an adversary specifies a vector $\mu = (\mu_1 \LDOTS \mu_k)$ of CTRs (concealed from \A), then for each agent $i$ and round $t$, \realization $\rho_i(t)$ is chosen independently with mean $\mu_i$. ... regret on this instance is defined as R^I(T) = T v_{i^*} \mu_{i^*} - E[ \sum_t \sum_i \mu_i v_i A_i(b;\rho;t) ].

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial MAB mechanism design problem (oblivious adversary)
unmapped: rewards are v_i * rho_i(t) with private values v_i in [0, v_max] reported as bids and clicks rho_i(t) in {0,1} chosen by an oblivious adversary
mechanism must be weakly truthful (truthful in expectation over its random seed for every click realization) and normalized
settings.definition_quote: The objective is to optimize the worst-case regret over all values v such that v_i in [0,Vmax] for each i, and all realizations rho: R(T;v;rho) = [max_i v_i sum_t rho_i(t)] - sum_t sum_i v_i rho_i(t) E[A_i(v;rho;t)]

source.label: thm:LB-main
source.quote: Consider the stochastic \problem\ with $k$ agents. Let \A\ be an exploration-separated deterministic allocation rule. Then its regret is $R(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\Vmax\, k^{1/3}\, T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Also stated in the introduction as Theorem 1.6 (normalized v_max). Applies to truthful normalized mechanisms with two agents (non-degenerate, scale-free) via the characterization, and to k agents under IIA.

source.label: thm:LB-delta
source.quote: In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:LB-main}, fix $k$ and $\Vmax$ and assume that $R(T;\, \Vmax) =O(\Vmax\, T^\gamma)$ for some $\gamma<1$. Then for every fixed $\delta\leq \tfrac14$ and $\lambda < 2(1-\gamma)$ we have $R_\delta(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\delta\,\Vmax\,T^\lambda)$.

results.notes: Worst case over delta-gap instances; recorded as instance_dependent. Theorem 1.6 states the same as Omega(delta T^{2(1-gamma)-eps}).

Suppose $\A$ satisfies IIA. Then its regret is $R(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\Vmax\, T^{2/3})$ for any sufficiently large $\Vmax$.

source.quote: Consider the stochastic \problem\ with $k$ agents. The naive mechanism is normalized,  truthful and has worst-case regret $R(T;\Vmax)= O(\Vmax\,  k^{1/3}\, T^{2/3}\, \log^{2/3} T)$.

results.notes: Mechanism is deterministic, truthful and normalized.

source.label: cor:weakly-truthful
source.quote: There exists a weakly truthful normalized mechanism for the adversarial MAB problem (against oblivious adversary) whose regret grows as $\bigo( (k\log k)^{1/3}\cdot T^{2/3}\cdot \vmax)$.

results.notes: Regret bound of PSim taken from Awerbuch-Kleinberg / Kleinberg lecture notes; novelty is the weakly truthful mechanism. Regret defined against best fixed agent in hindsight, expectation over mechanism randomness. Payments computation efficiency not claimed.
